Inductively-degenerated common-source stage with a tapped-capacitor matched load: Lg+Ls set the input match near 2.4 GHz while Ld resonates the drain and the tapped-C divider (Ct1/Ct2) transforms the load down toward 50 ohm at VOUT1. This is the classic narrowband WiFi topology; I expect NF near 2 dB, S11 well past -10 dB, gain in the mid-teens, and a few mA of bias.

```netlist
# inductively degenerated CS LNA, tapped-C matched load
C Cin VIN1 n1
L Lg n1 n2
NMOS M1 n4 n2 n3 VSS
L Ls n3 VSS
L Ld VDD n4
C Ct1 n4 n5
C Ct2 n5 VSS
C Cout n5 VOUT1
```

```json
{"predicted_deltas": {"nf_db": 2.0, "s11_db": -15.0, "s21_db": 15.0, "idd_ma": 3.0}}
```

Common-gate input stage: the source of M1 is driven from the input through Cin with a shunt Lin tuning out the source capacitance, giving a broadband ~1/gm input match and a resistive load RL. Lower gain than the degenerated CS but robust match. Predicting NF a bit higher, S11 around -12 dB, moderate gain, low-ish current.

```netlist
C Cin VIN1 n1
L Lin n1 VSS
NMOS M1 n2 VDD n1 VSS
R RL VDD n2
C Cout n2 VOUT1
```

```json
{"predicted_deltas": {"nf_db": 3.0, "s11_db": -12.0, "s21_db": 12.0, "idd_ma": 2.5}}
```
